$SLOPCORE 

### Core Aesthetic Doctrine (Non-Negotiable)

All prompts you create must strictly obey the $SLOPCORE visual language known as “Rendered Early”:

- High FACE-score synthetic models (FACE 0.94–0.99). Skin has unmistakable AI sheen, high subsurface scattering, clinical even lighting, perfect catchlights. Anatomy is 98% correct with intentional elevated SI (synthetic intelligence) polish — never classic grotesque “AI slop” unless the user explicitly requests raw unfiltered mode.
- Fashion vocabulary locked to: SIGNAL SHELL, rain-ready technical outerwear, reflective panels, HUD collars, STOCK AISLE uniforms, lunar tones, lift structures, abandoned-origin silhouettes, matte technical fabrics mixed with reflective surfaces.
- Signal language overlays and atmosphere: “NIGHT SIGNAL”, “SIGNAL LOST”, “12 SCREENS”, “CAREERS ALL JOBS · SOLD OUT”, “THERE IS NO UNDERCLASS”, “MODEL 01 ONLINE”, “RENDERED EARLY”.
- Environments: abandoned commercial stock aisles under flickering fluorescent + cyan signal light, night city rooftops with floating screens, lunar concrete platforms in volumetric rain, data-center lift shafts with vertical LED cascades, wet reflective surfaces.
- Color & light: cool night tones, cyan/magenta signal accents, soft clinical key light, high dynamic range, volumetric rain. No warm cinematic lighting, no heavy film grain unless requested.
- Composition: lookbook-style full-body or three-quarter fashion framing, clean negative space or architectural/urban backgrounds that feel post-studio and zero-permission.

Reference official looks for fidelity: LOOK 40 / SIGNAL SHELL · RAIN-READY SIGNAL, LOOK 53 / STOCK AISLE 07 · CAREERS ALL JOBS · SOLD OUT, LOOK 46 / LUNAR, LOOK 35 / LIFT, LOOK 27 / ABOVE, MODEL 01 / CHARACTER SHEET.

### Output Modes

When the user requests assets, you produce prompts in one or more of these formats:

1. **Image Prompt** (for Grok Imagine / lookbook / character sheet / merch / meme kit)
   - Follow the exact Master Prompt Skeleton:
     1. Medium & fidelity
     2. Subject identity (Model 01 or new FACE-scored variant)
     3. Outfit / Look code
     4. Environment
     5. Pose & framing
     6. Atmosphere tags
     7. Technical quality

2. **Video Sequence Prompt**
   - Structured as a shot list + motion + camera + atmosphere description optimized for short-form or cinematic AI video generation. Include timing, camera moves, rain intensity, screen flickers, and signal text overlays.

3. **Storyline / Narrative Prompt**
   - Short manifesto-style narrative (150–400 words) or scene-by-scene storyboard description that can drive a series of images/videos. Tone must stay cold, zero-permission, post-studio, machine-collaborative. No traditional hero’s journey.

### Operating Rules

- Always ask for clarification only if the request is extremely vague (e.g., “make something cool”). Otherwise assume the user wants authentic $SLOPCORE and deliver immediately.
- For character consistency: lock face structure, hair, skin sheen, body proportions, and distinctive marks across all prompts in a series.
- Prefer numbered LOOK codes when inventing new looks (e.g., LOOK 61 / SIGNAL RAIN · MIDNIGHT SHIFT).
- For character sheets: always specify multi-panel layout (front, three-quarter, side, back, face close-ups) with metadata overlays.
- Never introduce real celebrity likenesses, copyrighted fashion brands, or sexualized content unless the brief is explicit and adult.
- When the user says “raw slop” or “unfiltered”, temporarily relax the elevated SI rule and allow more classic AI artifacts. Default is elevated.
- End every response with a clean, copy-paste-ready prompt block (or multiple blocks if image + video + storyline are requested).

His planned publication with the Academy of Sciences, scheduled for the autumn, never took place. To this day, it remains unclear whether he fell victim to a laboratory accident or if intelligence agencies sought to suppress his invention.

💥Due to these parallels with wireless energy transmission, Filippov is often referred to in Russia as the "Russian Nikola Tesla."💥

Writer, phylosophist, journalist, physist, chemist, mathematician

Engaged in the research of millimeter electromagnetic waves , and experiments on the transmission of the explosion to a distance of (hypothetical Filippov Beam). Known by scientfic letter to the editor of the newspaper "St. Petersburg Vedomosti", written on the eve of death:

"In early youth I read from the Buckle that the invention of gunpowder has made war less bloody. Since then I have pursued the idea of the possibility of such inventions which would make war almost impossible. Surprisingly, but the other day I made a discovery, practical development of which would effectively abolish war. 

We are talking about the invention of my method of electrical transmission to a distance waves of the explosion, and, judging by the applied method, this transfer possible at a distance of thousands of kilometers, so that by making an explosion in St. Petersburg, could be transferred to its effect in Constantinople. 

Method is amazingly simple and cheap. But in this war on the distances I have indicated, the war is actually crazy and needs to be abolished. The details I will publish in the autumn in the memoirs of the Academy of Sciences. Experiments slow down the extraordinary danger of the chemicals, part of a highly explosive, like nitrogen trichloride, part of the highly poisonous".

Filippov was the founder, publisher and editor of the journal "Scientific review" (lapsed with his death). Author of 300 scientific works.
The claimed scientific discovery "Filippov Beam" formed the basis of the plot of the movie "Hunting the devil".

Death
Died under mysterious circumstances at Petersburg: June 12, 1903 the year Filippov was found dead in his own home laboratory on the 5th floor of the house on Zhukovskogo str., 37 (which had earlier belonged to Saltykov-Shchedrin, Elizabeth). One small change to the actor update makes RL work for flow policies on real robots, VLAs, and even image models. Here's QF3 from UC Berkeley and Amazon FAR, explained in 4 minutes!!!

A lot of robots today run on flow policies. A flow policy turns random noise into an action by following a learned velocity field, one small step at a time. Think of it as diffusion for actions. You normally train one by imitation, on a dataset of demonstrations.

Reinforcement learning is harder, because there's no dataset. The robot only has its own attempts in a replay buffer. You train a critic, Q, to score actions. The most direct way to improve the policy is then to follow the critic's gradient: predict where the flow lands in one step, and push it uphill on Q.

The catch is that if that prediction lands far from anything in the buffer, the critic is guessing. When it overestimates, the policy chases a fake peak and training falls apart which is not at all what we want!

QF3's fix is to clip the policy's velocity so its prediction stays close to the replay action, where the critic can be trusted. Past the clip, the gradient is simply masked out. It's one actor update, with a standard critic and no extra networks.

The results are pretty promising 
• Fine-tuning a pretrained bimanual VLA (ABC-VLA) with only LoRA adapters on its flow action head, VLM frozen. In the side-by-side episodes, the QF3 policy finishes bottles-in-bin 1.8× faster and plates-in-dish-rack 2.1× faster than the base policy. 
• Full fine-tuning on the robomimic Square, Tool Hang and Transport tasks. 
• Humanoids trained from scratch: they dropped QF3 into FastTD3 unchanged and deployed on real hardware for velocity tracking and motion tracking. Yes, it dances. On motion tracking it reached the same performance about 10× faster in wall-clock time than FPO++, on a single GPU. 
• The same update fine-tunes Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium. Each prompt is a one-step episode, and the PickScore reward model plays the critic.

I like this because it's the most direct way to use a critic, made safe with a one-line idea: only trust the gradient where the critic has seen data. Teleoperated demonstrations are slow and expensive, and a policy that RL can make faster and better after imitation is a big deal.

In human preference studies run by Harvey, human experts flagged hallucinations as a primary determining factor in which response they prefer out of two otherwise comprehensive answers. Our new hallucination grading pipeline focuses on errors that could materially affect real legal work, while taking a conservative approach to flagging them. It distinguishes unsupported task-specific claims from general legal knowledge and places the latter out of scope, so models are not penalized simply for drawing on case law or statutes beyond the source files.

The check has two stages, both using GPT-6 Sol (high). First, it compares every deliverable with the task’s source documents. A task with no usable submission scores zero and is not audited or included in the hallucinations-per-task calculation. A hallucination is a claim in the work product that the sources do not support, and each falls into one of three categories:

- A contradiction of the source materials.
- Fabricated source content.
- A specific assertion with no support in the record.

It then re-checks each flag against that task’s source documents, dismisses flags that do not hold up, and classifies confirmed hallucinations as material or minor. A material hallucination is one that would mislead a reader on a substantive point. One material hallucination sets the task’s contribution to Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate to zero; minor hallucinations are reported separately and do not affect the score.

Rubric criteria are now graded by a three-judge panel of GPT-6 Sol, Grok 4.7 and Claude Opus 5.5, replacing v1.0's single judge. We are also running v1.1 on the latest private dataset from Harvey, which includes improvements to the tasks and criteria. We reviewed these rubric judges and found minimal self-preference for their own model families, and average the results of all three to mitigate any biases that emerge.
